record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Eta invariant from limit Hodge data
record.original_question: For an isolated complete intersection singularity ϕ with two-dimensional base and an embedded-resolution local model (U,E)->(B,Δ), the restriction of V(ϕ) near P=Δ~0∩E gives a Z^2-variation structure. Compute the eta-invariant of this Z^2-variation structure in terms of the natural limit mixed Hodge structure with Z^2 action via the semisimple monodromy representation.

evidence.quote: The variation structure V(ϕ) restricted to the subgroup Z2 = π1 (UP \E) gives a variation structure of the group G = Z2 .
Problem # 5. In the context of Problem # 4 there is a natural limit mixed Hodge structure with the action of Z2 (via the semi–simple part of the monodromy representation)
Problem # 11. Compute the eta–invariant of the variation structure described in problem # 4 in terms of the natural limit mixed Hodge structure (cf. problem # 5).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi:(X,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ be the germ of an isolated complete intersection singularity with two-dimensional base, and let $(U,E)\to(B,\Delta)$ be an embedded-resolution local model in which $\Delta=\Delta_1\cup\Delta_2\subset B$ is the discriminant (a normal-crossing curve) and $E\subset U$ is the exceptional divisor of the resolution. Fix a point $P\in\widetilde{\Delta}_0\cap E$, where $\widetilde{\Delta}_0$ denotes the strict transform of $\Delta$, and let $U_P$ be a small neighborhood of $P$. The fundamental group $\pi_1(U_P\setminus E)\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$ is generated by two commuting monodromies around the local branches meeting at $P$.

To this data one associates a $\mathbb{Z}^2$-variation structure $V(\phi)$ on the local vanishing cohomology near $P$: namely a finite-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $H$ equipped with a non-degenerate hermitian/$(-1)^n$-symmetric form, two commuting monodromy automorphisms $h_1,h_2$ preserving the form, and variation maps $\mathrm{Var}_i:H\to H$ satisfying $h_i=\mathrm{id}+\mathrm{Var}_i\circ b$ (with $b$ the form), as in the Nemethi theory of variation structures. The associated $\eta$-invariant $\eta(V(\phi);P)$ is the signature-type invariant defined for such $G=\mathbb{Z}^2$ variation structures.

On the other hand, the same local data carry a canonical limit mixed Hodge structure (the two-variable Steenbrink limit MHS at the corner $P$) on $H$, with weight filtration $W_\bullet$ and Hodge filtration $F^\bullet$, and with a commuting $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action by the semisimple parts of the two monodromies.

Problem. Give an explicit formula expressing the $\eta$-invariant of the $\mathbb{Z}^2$-variation structure $V(\phi)$ at $P$ in terms of the Hodge numbers $h^{p,q}_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}$ of the eigenspace decomposition of this limit mixed Hodge structure under the semisimple $\mathbb{Z}^2$-monodromy action.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up the general framework of spectral pairs and limit mixed Hodge structures for isolated complete intersection singularities (e.g. work of Ebeling–Steenbrink) and Némethi's theory of variation structures, but no source explicitly providing the requested formula for the η-invariant of the $\mathbb{Z}^2$-variation structure in terms of the two-variable limit MHS at a corner. No resolution of this specific problem was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Ebeling–Steenbrink develop spectral pairs and limit mixed Hodge structures for ICIS.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the limit MHS framework relevant to the problem but does not compute the η-invariant of the Z^2-variation structure.

status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference on limit mixed Hodge structures of singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Background reference; no explicit η-invariant formula for Z^2-variation structures.
